question: Does a per-turn provenance stamp exist on conversation_messages, copied immutably into ledger rows (not session state), per A-10 as restructured by D-16?
root_cause: A provenance-shaped stamp DOES exist and IS written per-turn, but it lives in the same mutable conversation_messages.metadata_json column that the message row itself uses for everything else — there is no separate immutable ledger table. Per-turn write: onfinish_writethrough/run_adapter_dispatch builds `adapterLastAssistantMetadata.custom` = {model, queryId, planning_model_id, planning_latency_ms, disclosure_tier, query_class, stack, style, pipeline, conversationId} and conversation_writer.ts INSERTs it via `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET metadata_json = EXCLUDED.metadata_json` — i.e. the stamp is UPSERT-overwritable, not append-only/immutable. conversation_messages has exactly 7 columns (id, conversation_id, parent_message_id, role, parts_json, metadata_json, created_at) confirmed live against the DB — no dedicated provenance/build_id column, no separate ledger table exists anywhere in the schema (251-table survey by PG1-D1-0002 corroborated: no message_parts, and this lane found no *_ledger/*_provenance table for chat turns either).

evidence.quote:
const adapterLastAssistantMetadata: Record<string, unknown> = {
  custom: {
    model: modelId,
    queryId,
    planning_model_id: plannerModelId,

    disclosure_tier: audienceTier,

columns: id uuid, conversation_id uuid, parent_message_id uuid, role text, parts_json jsonb, metadata_json jsonb, created_at timestamptz -- no version/provenance/build_id column, no separate ledger table

residual_unknown: Whether D-16's restructured A-10 intends 'immutable ledger row' to literally require a separate append-only table (in which case this is a real gap to build) or whether an UPSERT-but-never-actually-updated-in-practice column satisfies the spirit of the requirement (in which case it's a naming/documentation gap, not a build gap). conversation_messages currently has 0 live rows in this DB instance, so this lane could not observe whether metadata_json is ever actually overwritten in production traffic (e.g. on regenerate) versus only ever written once per row.
recommended_action: If D-16's intent is a true immutable ledger, add a dedicated `conversation_message_provenance` (or similar) append-only table keyed by message_id + written_at, populated at the same write-through call site (run_adapter_dispatch.ts:472) instead of/in addition to metadata_json. If the intent is already satisfied by 'never actually re-updated in practice', document that explicitly since the schema as written does not enforce it.

question: When chart_id is omitted entirely (or sent null/empty) at the REST layer beneath the MCP client, does the platform reject the call, or does a default/native chart UUID leak in?
root_cause: The underlying REST endpoint the MCP server proxies to is POST /api/retrieval/capability (platform/src/app/api/retrieval/capability/route.ts). This lane could not reach it via live raw HTTP — no dev server is running in this worktree, no PLATFORM_URL/DB credentials are configured locally (platform-mcp defaults to http://localhost:3000, nothing listening), and no deployed staging URL was available to this diagnostic seat, so genuine outside-the-MCP-client HTTP could not be executed here (a real, documented gap — see residual_unknown). In its place this lane did a decisive source read of the exact code path a raw HTTP call would hit: for scope='per_chart' capabilities, chart_id is resolved ONLY from `args['chart_id']` (typeof check) or the `X-MCP-Chart-Id` header, defaulting to `null` if both are absent — never to NATIVE_CHART_ID or any other fallback. If null, the route returns `400 {error_class:'validation', message:'CHART_REQUIRED', ...}` before any handler runs (fail-closed). This is corroborated by a second, independent defense layer: several individual capability handlers (dprofiles_registration.ts:119, register_d6_synergy.ts:103/216, router_registration.ts:89) each re-check `if (!chart_id || typeof chart_id !== 'string')` and reject on their own, so even a hypothetical bypass of the route-level gate would be caught at the handler. A dedicated, FROZEN CI gate (chart_agnostic_gate.ts, D1 contract) also statically forbids any per_chart capability from declaring a `default` on its chart_id input_schema field (Rule 4) or omitting chart_id from required_inputs (Rule 1) — invoked live via `npx tsx chart_agnostic_gate.ts`, which ran and printed PASS, though with 0 capabilities checked because the registry singleton isn't populated outside the Next.js request-time bootstrap (a residual noted below, not a pass/fail signal on its own).

residual_unknown: True raw-HTTP-from-outside-the-MCP-client execution (curl against a live deployed instance) was not performed — this diagnostic worktree has no running server, no DATABASE_URL/PLATFORM_URL configured, and no reachable staging/production base URL was located. A future lane with either (a) a running local dev server with real env vars, or (b) network access to a deployed instance, should re-run this as literal `curl -X POST .../api/retrieval/capability -d '{"uri":...,"args":{}}'` (omitting chart_id and the X-MCP-Chart-Id header) to get a live HTTP 400 observation rather than a code-path inference. question: §19 P5' assumes a queryable citation/message_parts linkage ranking signal_ids by citation frequency. Is the actual persisted shape 'no citations exist' or 'citations exist in a different, non-obvious shape'?
root_cause: Different shape, confirmed by source read. Citations are NOT stored as structured child rows (message_parts does not exist — reconfirmed, see PG1-D1-0002) and are NOT recorded under the key names PG-1 scanned for as literal JSON keys inside parts_json in the way expected. The actual mechanism: platform/src/lib/citations/citation_data_part.ts defines a `CitationPart` = {type:'citation', index, signal_id: /^SIG\.MSR\.\d{3}$/, layer:'L1'|'L2.5', snippet}, produced by `extractCitations()` scanning the assistant's rendered text for `SIG\.MSR\.\d{3}` patterns and de-duplicating in order of first appearance — these CitationPart objects are emitted as a distinct AI-SDK data-part type from the consume route's onFinish handler and would be embedded inside the message's `parts_json` array (as one of the array's part objects, field name literally `signal_id`) rather than in any separate table. PG-1's ILIKE scan for the literal string 'signal_id' over parts_json should therefore have matched real citation parts if any existed. It found 0. This lane independently re-ran the same scan live against the DB and also found 0 matches — but discovered why: conversation_messages has exactly 0 rows and conversations has exactly 1 row in this DB instance. PG-1's 0-match result is not evidence citations never fire in production; it is an artifact of this DB instance having essentially no real conversational traffic to sample.

question: Does batch-resolution / compliance-decay / lapsing logic exist for prediction outcome tracking, per assumption A-31 ('Compliance decay is designed for: batch resolution, LEL-drafted outcomes, non-shameful lapsing, coverage reported alongside every score', §14.7)?
root_cause: No such mechanism exists. Grepped platform/src and platform-mcp/src for batch/decay/lapse/expire/auto-resolve/stale/deadline in the outcome-recording code paths (mimamsa_outcome.ts, ppl_writer.ts) — zero matches. The DB carries two independent prediction-tracking systems, neither of which has an automatic lapsing/decay mechanic: (1) `mcp_predictions`/`mcp_prediction_outcomes` — a manual verified:boolean + outcome_text/outcome_notes pair, populated only by an explicit outcome-recording call, no expiry column. (2) `mimamsa_predictions` — carries `observation_window` (daterange) and `eval_date`, which look like they COULD drive an auto-lapse job, but `lifecycle_status`'s only defined values (platform/src/lib/lel/prospective_ledger.ts:81) are `'open' | 'matched' | 'confirmed' | 'falsified' | 'withdrawn'` — no 'lapsed'/'expired' state exists in the type, and the only code that transitions lifecycle_status (prospective_ledger.ts:449, on an explicit event-candidate match) does so per-row on manual match, never as a batch sweep over rows whose observation_window has closed. A repo-wide search for cron/scheduled-job infrastructure found only an unrelated aiops health-probe cron (`probe_health_cron.ts`) and an `/api/admin/cron` route — neither touches predictions.

WHERE chart_id = $1::uuid AND event_class = $2 AND lifecycle_status = 'open'
columns include observation_window (daterange), eval_date (date), lifecycle_status (text) -- no expiry/decay flag column

residual_unknown: Whether an auto-lapse sweep is planned-but-unbuilt (a natural fit given observation_window/eval_date already exist) vs. deliberately never intended (predictions stay 'open' forever pending manual resolution) was not determinable from code/schema alone — no design doc reference to A-31's exact phrase was located during this probe.
recommended_action: If A-31 describes intended target-state behavior, this is a real build gap: a scheduled job that flips `lifecycle_status` to a new 'lapsed' value (schema migration required — the enum-like type would need extending) when `observation_window`'s upper bound passes with no match/confirmation/falsification. Recommend routing to whichever workstream owns mimamsa_predictions calibration for sizing.
